prova:
by
  haveI : Fintype (SimpleGraph (Fin 5)) := SimpleGraph.fintype
  haveI : DecidableRel (fun (u v : Fin 5) => u = v) := inferInstance
  haveI : DecidableEq (SimpleGraph (Fin 5)) := SimpleGraph.decidableEqFin
  haveI : DecidablePred (fun (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)) => G.CliqueFree 3) := fun G => inferInstance
  haveI (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)) : DecidablePred (fun (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)) => H ≤ G) := fun H => inferInstance
  haveI (G H : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)) : Decidable (H.IsBipartite) := inferInstance
  have dec_prop : Decidable (∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)),
        H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ 1) := inferInstance
  cases dec_prop with
  | isTrue h => exact h
  | isFalse h =>
      exfalso
      -- If false, there is a counterexample, but we can verify by decide that all satisfy the property.
      -- Wait, if `dec_prop` is `isFalse`, we can just use `decide` on the universal quantification if we formulate it as a boolean.
      have : (∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)),
        H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ 1) := by decide
      contradiction
